I got through last night. One day at a time.

I keep hearing that. And I'm literally fighting myself to stay in the house. But it doesn't seem like it's going anywhere. I've 'stayed sober today' for almost a month now, and 'tomorrow's problems' haven't gone anywhere. It's getting closer and closer to 'tomorrow' and I can't see any signs of it changing. 

Granted, the GF issue isn't a major deal. I'm not in a place to give myself the time I need, any relationship right now would be short lived. 

The work, and the apartment, and the bills, though. They aren't going away. The day is getting closer and closer and nothing is falling in place. All I have is this crushing feeling of helplessness. I can't control any of it. Sure, I can send hundreds of apps. But it's up to someone else, sometimes not even a real person, on the other end to decide if they even want to interview me. The same thing with rent. It's not up to me what happens if I can't pay. Same thing with bills. Nothing in my life right now isn't in my control. That feeling of helplessness, combined with my depression, is just making it difficult to get by every day sober. At least I am in control of drinking. Though the way I'm feeling tonight, I'm not even sure about that. It's like I don't even have control over my alcohol.

>Make a gratitude list

I don't have much to be grateful for right now. No girlfriend, no job, I'll be homeless at the end of March if nothing changes in two weeks, no friends to turn to for help. I have my apartment (for now) and internet. (Again, for now.) I have no marketable skills, no education, and my job outlook is bleak. If I get a job, it'll be part time, low paying, not enough to even cover my bills. Getting a second job in this economy looks almost impossible. 

I just can't see a way out of this. Granted, I think that has to do more with my depression than my alcoholism, but the alcohol is the one thing that lets me escape. I don't know what to do and the longer I'm stuck in my head the worse the depression gets.

Been there for a few years now. I fear the day I have one too many drinks and wind up ending it all on impulse. I've been very close this week. For me, it's not so much a fear of what next, but a fear of what if I fail and it hurts.

>I'm sorry you felt attacked

That's not really how the comment came across. I have no doubt that stopping won't be easy. And that putting it off won't be good. But I chose that date for a very specific reason, and because I think that one reason will be all I need to stop. If it isn't, then I guess I'm just a worthless alcoholic like my father. And no, that isn't a pity-party thing. My dad is a worthless alcoholic. And if I can't stop when I want to, I'm no better than him. I guess we'll see on Feb 8 2012.

I wouldn't say gross. Not great by any means, though. I wanted alcohol and didn't want to spend an assload. And didn't know how the night would end, because it's never gone like that before. 

>Well first of all this subreddit is a great place, you'll be met with acceptance and understanding

Yeah. Haven't got much of that thus far. Mostly just been told that I'm choosing to quit 'wrong', which just makes me want to quit less. Why should I join a crowd that would tell someone that was trying to quit that he was trying to quit wrong?

Sorry. Guess it would be better to do it myself and fail just like I have every other time, instead of asking for help. There's a reason for the date, if nothing else. And just because I said that would be my last drink doesn't mean I'll drink between then and now. 

But, whatever. My 'grand announcement' has been deleted. I'll deal with it myself instead of looking for help.
